title: access-telescoping-gap-mapping-auditor-qa
content:
Purpose:
This working brief maps RBAC v2, audit log schema, SIEM export, and evidence automation to SOC 2 / ISO 27001 control areas, surfaces gaps we should fix before the next auditor interview, and provides a short Q&A cheat sheet for on-the-spot auditor questions.

Scope:
- RBAC v2 (role model, change processes, delegated admin, emergency/break-glass)
- Audit log schema (producer-level fields, integrity, retention)
- SIEM export pipeline (ETL, normalization, enrichment, retention/archival)
- Evidence automation (ingest validations, manifests, proofs)

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We are largely aligned with the SOC 2/ISO requirements for access control and logging, but several pragmatic gaps remain for a clean auditor walkthrough: (1) audit log schema misses explicit token/session linkage for service-to-service events; (2) RBAC change approval evidence is scattered (PRs + Slack approvals) and not consistently retained in a single evidence store; (3) SIEM export pipeline lacks automated schema validation and manifesting for long-term retention; (4) evidence automation does not yet generate tamper-evident manifests for exported evidence bundles. Each gap has a prioritized remediation and an evidence checklist below.

Control mapping highlights (high-level):
- SOC 2 (Security category): access provisioning, least privilege, change authorization, logging/monitoring maps to RBAC v2 + audit logs + SIEM exports.
- ISO 27001 (Annex A): A.9 (Access control), A.12 (Operations and communications), A.16 (Information security incident management) — our RBAC, runtime logs, and SIEM pipeline provide the primary evidence.

Current state summary (short bullets):
- RBAC v2: role catalog implemented; role inheritance and attribute-based overrides available; no centralized attestation records; emergency roles exist but break-glass activation logs are sparse.
- Audit logs: comprehensive event stream for user-facing actions; fields: timestamp, user_id, action, resource_id, resource_type, outcome, request_id. Missing: session_id, token_id, model_id/model_version metadata for inference calls.
- SIEM export: daily batch export to SIEM; enrichment jobs attach geo/ip context; export manifests are manual; no per-export checksum or signed manifest.
- Evidence automation: partial; PR-based evidence ingestion exists but manual tags required to associate PRs to control IDs.

Gap analysis (detailed, with impact and recommended remediation):
1) Missing session/token linkage in audit schema
   - Impact: Can't unambiguously link machine-to-machine inference requests to an identity for auditing or repro. Auditor will ask for end-to-end traceability.
   - Remediation: Add token_id and session_id fields in the audit producer (serving runtime) and update ingestion mapping. Backfill recent 30-day logs with correlation keys where possible. Owner: Serving runtime (Marcus). Priority: high. Target ETA: 4 weeks.

2) Sparse break-glass evidence
   - Impact: Emergency access is used but approval / post-facto review evidence is inconsistent. Could fail ISO attestation for control over privileged access.
   - Remediation: Implement automated ticket creation on break-glass activation (create CT- incident ticket with fields: activator, reason, duration, CCR reviewer). Retain artifacts in evidence bucket. Owner: SRE/Platform (Diego). Priority: medium. ETA: 3 weeks for ticket wiring; 6 weeks for retention automation.

3) SIEM export manifests not machine-verified
   - Impact: Auditors expect chain-of-custody (file hashes, signed manifests) for evidence retention. Manual manifests increase chance of missing exports.
   - Remediation: Add manifest generator to export pipeline that writes a signed manifest per export (sha256 hashes, record count, export window) to s3://redwood-audit-manifests/, and inject manifest reference into Confluence attestation record. Owner: Observability (Priya). Priority: high. ETA: 2 weeks.

4) Evidence linking across systems is ad hoc
   - Impact: When asked to show role change -> approval -> deployment -> log of privileged action, we currently stitch artifacts from GitHub PR, Slack thread, and audit logs manually.
   - Remediation: Define a canonical evidence correlation ID pattern (e.g., EVID-YYYY-XXXX) that is added to PR descriptions, approval tickets, and export manifests. Build a lightweight evidence search page in Console. Owner: Security Platform. Priority: medium. ETA: 6-8 weeks.

Remediation tracker (quick view):
- Token/session fields: Marcus (serving-runtime) — high — 4w
- Manifest generator: Priya (observability) — high — 2w
- Break-glass ticketing: Diego (sre/platform) — medium — 3-6w
- Evidence correlation ID + Console index: Security Platform — medium — 6-8w

Evidence pack checklist (what to present to an auditor today):
- RBAC artifacts: role definition spreadsheet (roles.csv), role change PRs (link list), current role->permission snapshot (roles-snapshot-2025-02-01.json).
- Approval evidence: PR review threads, Confluence policy doc for RBAC v2, selected access request tickets.
- Logs: example raw audit file (audit-2025-02-10-00.json.gz) showing user actions; mapping doc that explains each field.
- SIEM exports: last 7 daily export manifests (manual for now), enrichment job logs, SIEM ingestion confirmation screenshots.
- Evidence automation: ingestion runbook, S3 bucket policy, retention settings.

Suggested auditor Q&A (scripted answers + artifact references):
Q: How do you ensure only authorized people can elevate privileges?
A: RBAC v2 enforces least privilege via role assignments; elevation requests require a ticket and two-step approval (PR + manager approval) for roles with admin scopes. See roles.csv (artifact) + ticket CT-4302 (artifact).

Q: Show me proof that a break-glass event was reviewed after the fact.
A: Provide break-glass activation log entry (audit-2025-01-15), the automatically generated incident ticket CT-5121 with post-mortem, and the reviewer sign-off in Confluence (page: Break-glass-review-2025-01). If missing, note remediation: we will wire automatic ticket generation within 3 weeks.

Q: How do logs propagate to your SIEM and how do you verify exports?
A: Logs are published to s3://redwood-audit-raw/ then an ETL job normalizes events and writes daily bundles to s3://redwood-audit-siementry/. Each export includes an export manifest (manual today) and is ingested to the SIEM. We will soon generate signed manifests (artifact: export-manifest-spec.md).

Q: Can you show an end-to-end trace linking a privileged API call back to the identity that initiated it?
A: For human-initiated actions yes (user_id + request_id). For service-to-service inference calls, we currently lack token_id in logs — remediation planned. For the auditor, we can demonstrate recent examples where request_id + IP + model request meta allow confident linkage and show the PR for adding token_id.

Packaging & demo notes (how to run a short evidence walkthrough):
1) Start with roles.csv and point to the role snapshot in the Console.
2) Show a role change PR and the associated approval ticket.
3) Pull the raw audit file that contains the action being audited. Use the mapping doc to point out each field.
4) Show the SIEM export directory and the manual manifest for context.
5) If asked about missing items (token_id or signed manifests), state the planned ETA and reference JIRA tickets.

Quick wins (deliverables before auditor arrival):
- Add token_id and session_id to audit producers and add basic backfill for last 30 days (high impact).
- Add signed manifests for daily SIEM exports (low effort).
- Create an evidence pack template per control with expected artifact IDs and example file names (medium effort).

Open questions for reviewers (please add inline comments):
- Do we have retention exceptions for debug logs that could conflict with ISO retention requirements?
- Are there any legal/regulatory holds that should override automated deletion for certain customers?
- Who will take ownership of the evidence correlation ID index in Console?

Appendix (short references to internal artifacts to attach to final evidence pack):
- roles.csv (latest)
- roles-snapshot-2025-02-01.json
- audit-log-schema-v2.md (producer schema reservoir)
- export-manifest-spec.md
- break-glass-runbook.md (draft)
- JIRA-SC-1821 (token/session audit fields)

Notes to reviewer: this is a working draft intended to be used by the security-on-call during auditor interviews. Please mark any regulatory nuances or missing legal constraints in comments.

Prepared by: Amina Patel (security) — contact: amina.patel@redwood.ai
